Subject: Cedar POC: burst capacity & success criteria

Hi Alicia / Ben — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment on scope and compute for the POC.

Call recap (30m):
- Goal: Validate real-time triage pipeline on ~2k monthly active sessions, measure 95th pct latency under 500ms for core inference path, and confirm cost-per-call estimates.
- Test data: 1k sample conversations + anonymized production traces (you agreed to share a 24h traffic slice).
- Success criteria (tentative):
  - Latency: 95th <= 500ms for 512-token average requests
  - Throughput: sustained 60 req/s with peak bursts to 140 req/s for ~5 minutes
  - Stability: <0.5% error rate for endpoint failures during a 48h soak
  - Quality: end-to-end task accuracy within 3% of current baseline

Capacity asks / constraints you mentioned:
- Reserved GPUs preferred for predictable bursts (NVIDIA A100 equivalent)
- Procurement lead time may be 2–3 weeks for contract sign-off
- Env: VPC peering for private trial; no production data to leave VPC

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm owners):
1) Cedar: share 24h traffic slice + success-priority list (Alicia) — by EOD Thu 5/20
2) Redwood SE (Neha): produce a POC compute map (reserved GPUs + autoscale plan) and rough cost estimate — by Tue 5/24 (attached draft model)
3) Redwood CS (Marissa): propose pilot runbook and monitoring dashboard access; schedule canary run window — by Wed 5/25
4) Procurement: confirm contract milestone for reserved capacity (Ben / procurement) — target week of 5/31

I attached a short template for the traffic slice and a starter compute question list in-line below. If that timeline looks good I’ll lock calendar for a 30m ops kickoff next week.

Thanks,

Thanks Sean — that recap is right. Quick clarifications from our side:

- We can provide an anonymized 24h trace by tomorrow EOD (5/19) rather than Thu. Will include request/response size histogram and token distributions.
- Our expected baseline is ~40 req/s sustained during business hours with periodic spikes up to ~160 req/s during claims processing windows (spikes typically last 3–7 minutes).
- Primary success metric for Cedar product team: 95th latency under 500ms for the API path that includes a lightweight NLU layer + Redwood model call.
- Secondary constraint: any solution must be able to fail-open to a smaller fallback model to keep the UI responsive if higher-tier GPUs are constrained.

Ownership: I will own providing traces and business success criteria (Alicia). Ben will coordinate procurement timelines; I’ll loop procurement once we have an estimate from Redwood.

One ask: can you include an autoscaling policy that allows short bursts to 200 req/s for up to 10 minutes with controlled cooldowns (we need to simulate a major batch window)? If this adds a lot of cost, flag it in the estimate.

Thanks — I put together an initial compute plan and a few configuration options. See attached: redwood_poc_compute_estimate.pdf and a mapping workbook cedar_poc_map.xlsx. High level notes below.

Summary (short):
- Baseline reserved pool: 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) — supports ~60 sustained req/s with target 95th latency headroom to 450ms for 512-token avg.
- Burst policy: allow horizontal scale to 10x GPUs for short windows (auto-burst), which covers ~160–200 req/s peaks. Burst target should be capped via policy to avoid runaway costs.
- Warm KV / prefix cache: we recommend pre-warming KV cache using a 24h sample to reduce first-token latency in cold-starts; low-cost NVMe cache nodes for hot prefixes.
- Canary plan: 6-hour canary (live traffic 5% routed) then 48-hour soak at 25% traffic before full POC run.

Costs / trade-offs:
- Option A (Reserved-first): 4 reserved GPUs + burst to 10 via autoscale. Predictable monthly base, moderate burst cost.
- Option B (On-demand heavy burst): 0 reserved, 10 on-demand during peak — cheaper baseline, expensive and unpredictable bursts. Not recommended for your uptime SLA.

Technical details to confirm from Cedar:
1) Typical sequence length distribution (we expect mean ~280 tokens, max 1200)
2) Allowed data egress constraints for cache warming (you said VPC-only)
3) Any required HSM/KMS integration for key material

Attached files:
- redwood_poc_compute_estimate.pdf (line-item cost for reserved + burst scenarios)
- cedar_poc_map.xlsx (mapping of Cedar traffic classes to test plan and priority endpoints)

If you can confirm (1)-(3) and the procurement lead-time window, I’ll convert this to a formal reserved-capacity quote and a signed SOW draft.

Thanks — I left some inline comments in the workbook on warmup windows and cache sizing.

—Neha
